issues.legal_issue: A written reconveyance understanding was genuine and binding because it was signed by an authorized agent and supported by the parties’ conduct.
material_facts: The seller and the purchaser’s husband recorded terms requiring reconveyance if the purchase price was repaid within three years, together with an additional amount for improvements.
The document was signed by agents for both sides rather than by the principals themselves.
A later letter referred to the understanding, and one of the two properties was reconveyed within the stated period for a price consistent with the recorded terms.
The evidence showed that the person who signed for the purchaser’s side was her husband’s employee and that her husband played the leading role in the transactions and acted on her behalf.
issues.conclusion: The written understanding was genuine, and the agent’s act bound the defendants; the understanding was enforceable against them.
issues.legal_principle: Acts performed by an agent within the agent’s authority bind the principal. The Court assessed the evidence as a whole, including the document, the subsequent correspondence and transaction, and the parties’ conduct. It referred to Gopalakrishnaji v. Mohammed Hazi Latiff on drawing an adverse inference when a party withholds the best evidence, but resolved the agency question on the evidence led rather than by drawing that inference.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and written_repurchase_terms and authorized_agent_signed and subsequent_transaction_consistent

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: A claimant brings a proceeding seeking performance of an alleged agreement to reconvey property.
predicates.written_repurchase_terms: The parties’ written record sets out terms under which property is to be reconveyed after repayment of the purchase price.
predicates.authorized_agent_signed: A person acting with authority for a contracting party signs the written record.
predicates.subsequent_transaction_consistent: The parties later engage in a transaction consistent with the written reconveyance terms.

issues.definition: When a reconveyance claim rests on written repurchase terms signed by an authorized agent and the parties’ later transaction is consistent with those terms, the understanding is treated as genuine and binding.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court reversing a trial court’s factual finding must engage with the trial court’s reasons for that finding.
material_facts: The trial court found that the person who signed the reconveyance document was an agent of the defendants, relying on several circumstances.
The appellate bench discussed some of those circumstances but did not address all of the trial court’s reasons.
The Supreme Court concluded that the appellate bench had not adequately dealt with the trial court’s reasoning before reversing its finding.
issues.conclusion: Before reversing a factual finding, an appellate court must bear in mind and address the reasons given by the trial court; the reversal in this case could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that an appellate court reviewing factual findings must engage with the reasoning of the court below. It relied on Dollar Co. v. Collector of Madras and the Privy Council’s decision in Rani Hemant Kumari v. Maharaja Jagadhindra Nath.

predicates.appeal_from_trial_factual_findings: A party appeals a trial court’s factual finding.
predicates.appellate_court_reverses_finding: The appellate court reverses the trial court’s factual finding.
predicates.appellate_court_ignores_material_trial_r: The appellate court fails to address material reasons the trial court gave for its finding.

issues.definition: If an appellate court reverses a trial court’s factual finding without addressing material reasons supporting it, the reversal should not stand.

issues.legal_issue: A sufficiently definite agreement intended to create an obligation is enforceable even if the parties describe it as a gentleman’s understanding.
material_facts: The written record described the arrangement as a gentleman’s understanding but specified the repayment period, the repayment amount, and an additional amount relating to improvements.
The agents for both sides executed the document, and the parties’ conduct, including the reconveyance of another property, was consistent with the stated arrangement.
issues.conclusion: The parties intended to create a legal obligation, and the agreement was an enforceable contract on which specific performance could be sought.
issues.legal_principle: A valid and enforceable contract is the basis for jurisdiction to order specific performance. The Court relied on Mayawanti v. Kaushalya Devi and Commissioner of Wealth Tax, Bhopal v. Abdul Hussain Mulla Mohammad Ali, and distinguished Rose and Frank Co. v. J.R. Crompton & Bros. Ltd. and Annapoorani Ammal v. G. Thangapalam. It held that the label attached to the arrangement did not negate the legal obligation created by definite terms and the parties’ intention that they be acted upon.

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: A claimant brings a proceeding seeking performance of an alleged agreement to reconvey property.
predicates.definite_reconveyance_terms: The agreement specifies the conditions and terms for reconveyance of the property.
predicates.parties_intended_to_be_bound: The parties’ conduct and the execution of the agreement show that they intended to create an obligation to be acted upon.

issues.definition: An agreement sought to be specifically enforced is enforceable when it states definite reconveyance terms and the parties intended those terms to bind them.

issues.legal_issue: Delay caused by litigation, increased property value, and a disclosed assignment made for pressing reasons do not necessarily justify refusing specific performance when the assignment is not champertous and the opposing party has acted unfairly.
material_facts: The suit had been pending for decades, and the property’s value had risen during the litigation; the delay was not attributed to an act of the plaintiff.

The plaintiff’s legal representatives assigned their rights to third parties during the appeal, disclosed the assignment to the Court, and the assignment deeds indicated pressing reasons for the transfer.
The defendants had denied the reconveyance understanding and had not complied with the trial judge’s wish that the relevant employee be examined as a court witness.
The Court found no basis to characterize the assignment in this case as a purchase of litigation amounting to champerty.
issues.conclusion: The Court exercised its discretion to grant specific performance; the delay, rise in value, and assignment did not warrant refusing relief in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 20(1), (2)(c), and (3) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, the discretion to order specific performance is judicial rather than arbitrary, and inequity may justify refusal. Delay not caused by the claimant and ordinary property-value increases during litigation should not normally defeat relief; the Court invoked actus curiae neminem gravabit and relied on S. V. Sankaralinga Nagar v. P.I.S. Ratnaswami Nadar and Abdul Hakeem Khan v. Abdul Menon Khadri. An assignment akin to champerty may justify, and should lead to, refusal of relief, but an assignee may be a representative in interest under Section 15(b); the Court relied on T.M. Balakrishna Mudaliar v. M. Satyanarayana Rao.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and enforceable_repurchase_agreement and delay_not_caused_by_claimant and property_value_increased_during_litigation and assignment_disclosed and assignment_for_pressing_reasons and not assignment_champertous and opposing_party_acted_unfairly

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: A claimant brings a proceeding seeking performance of an agreement to reconvey property.
predicates.enforceable_repurchase_agreement: The parties made an enforceable agreement for repurchase or reconveyance of the property.
predicates.delay_not_caused_by_claimant: The claimant did not cause the delay in resolving the proceeding.
predicates.property_value_increased_during_litigati: The property increased in value while the proceeding was pending.
predicates.assignment_disclosed: The claimant’s successor disclosed the assignment of the contractual right to the court.
predicates.assignment_for_pressing_reasons: The assignment was made for pressing reasons rather than merely to speculate on the litigation.
predicates.assignment_champertous: The assignment amounts to a champertous purchase of the litigation.
predicates.opposing_party_acted_unfairly: The party resisting relief acted unfairly in the dispute or in the conduct of the proceeding.

issues.definition: When an enforceable repurchase agreement is pursued without claimant-caused delay, property-value increases occur during litigation, and a disclosed assignment is made for pressing reasons rather than as a champertous purchase, unfair conduct by the opposing party supports granting specific performance.
